controls.conclusion: The name scanner detects its direct positive control and misses four file-I/O spellings. It does not prove absence of disk I/O.

The seeded float stream contains NaNs and subnormals but neither infinity nor signed zero. Infinity has separate hard-coded special vectors; negative-zero truthiness is a separate RAWS example, not a float-rendering sample.
Any finite prefix/held-out agreement can be shared by an extension that violates the proposed all-n recurrence; additional generative premises are necessary.

Changing data and its co-stored digest preserves local consistency. A hash detects drift relative to a separately retained expected digest; it does not prove historical immutability or time of origin.
The page's second suggested exercise only exposes a problem if replacement order is reversed; data-first then question preserves the inserted ${data} in the question.

controls.limits: Odd-cycle population is exhaustive. Integer optimality globally follows odd parity of 1-2c and witnesses0,1, not just the bounded enumeration. No production geometry or physics checker invoked.

limits: Only the reviewed scanner function is loaded through an AST extraction. Planted code is parsed, never executed.
Other controls are independent finite calculations, not new production verifier/test-suite replays.
